title: LED with resistor
probe1: LED anode: the row between the resistor and the LED
notes: probe1_row is a placeholder until docs/HARDWARE.md lists the real probe rows.

mistakes.hint: Current is almost zero, but the LED row still has full voltage. LEDs only let current flow one way. Look at its two legs.
mistakes.explain: The LED is in backwards. The longer leg (anode, +) must face the resistor and 5 V; the shorter leg (cathode, -) goes to ground. Flip it around.

mistakes.description: No resistor, LED connected straight to 5 V
mistakes.hint: Power was cut because the current was far too high. What part in the circuit limits how much current flows through the LED?
mistakes.explain: The LED was connected straight to 5 V with no resistor. Without a resistor nothing limits the current, so it rushes far past what the LED can take and burns it out. Put the 220 ohm resistor between 5 V and the LED's long leg.

mistakes.description: Circuit is not closed (part in the wrong row)
mistakes.hint: No current and no voltage at the LED. Something is not connected. Check that each leg is in the row you think it is.
mistakes.explain: The circuit is not a closed loop. Each part must share a row with the next part: 5 V to resistor, resistor to the LED's long leg, LED's short leg to ground. The lit row shows where the probe is; make sure the resistor and LED both reach it.
